gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only plug-in solar battery it showed for the US, the EcoFlow STREAM Ultra, puts out at most 800 W to the grid on its own (the 1,200 W figure needs a separate STREAM Microinverter or 2–6 Ultra units), lists UL 1741/IEEE 1547 rather than the UL 3700 plug-in PV certification that SB 868 points to, and is sold for plug-and-play installation in Utah only. That leaves a plain power station with portable panels as the battery setup a California shopper can actually buy.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited: californiabalconysolar.com/sb-868, pluginsolartracker.com/…/california and the KQED 2026-09-30 article. All three give the 1,200 W AC per-dwelling cap and a UL/equivalent 'plug-in PV system' certification, and none of them covers batteries. None names a product. KQED does say in general terms that 'currently available products do not yet meet the outlined requirements', which counts as part of the finding and is why this scores 2, not 3. No rival page gives the STREAM Ultra's 800 W standalone limit, its certification set or its Utah-only sale. No rival page puts power-station specs on the same basis, for example Anker comparing its own 4,000 cycles to 80% with a rival's 4,000 cycles to 70%.
decides: For a US (California) shopper, this rules out the grid-tied battery that ChatGPT led with. On EcoFlow's own US page, the STREAM Ultra is sold for Utah only and lists no plug-in PV certification. The pick then comes from off-grid power stations with portable panels. Compared on the same basis: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W at $1,499 (2,073.6–2,080 Wh, 2,600 W, 1,000 W solar input); BLUETTI AC180 at $499 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 500 W solar, out of stock until late November); Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, 800 W solar, 4,000 cycles to 80%). One caveat: SB 868's 1,200 W cap covers AC output fed into the home's wiring. A power station that only runs appliances from its own outlets is the separate off-grid route, so these continuous ratings are not held to that cap.

findings.value: 800 W standalone; the 1,200 W maximum needs the STREAM Microinverter or 2–6 Ultra units
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: Headline 'Max. 1200W', footnote 1: 'A single EcoFlow STREAM Ultra (standalone) has a max. 800W On-Grid AC output.'

findings.label: US sale restriction
findings.value: Sold for sale and plug-and-play installation in Utah only
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: Footnote 6: 'this product is only available for sale and plug-and-play installation in Utah.'

findings.label: Certifications listed
findings.value: UL 1741 and IEEE 1547; UL 3700 and UL 9540 not listed
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: UL 1741 covers grid-interactive inverters. SB 868 requires certification 'as a plug-in photovoltaic system'; see the UL 3700 finding.

findings.label: Battery and solar input
findings.value: 1.92 kWh per unit (scalable to 11.52 kWh), LFP, 6,000 cycles with no retention % given; 2,000 W solar input
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Series Plug-and-Play Home Solar System
findings.note: Appliances plugged straight into the Ultra must have a surge below 1,200 W (page footnote).

findings.label: Plug-in PV certification standard
findings.value: UL 3700, the Outline of Investigation for Interactive Plug-In Photovoltaic Equipment and Systems, program launched 2026-01-08; no wattage limit and no battery coverage in the release
findings.source_title: UL Solutions Debuts Testing and Certification Framework for Safer Plug-In Solar Across the United States
findings.note: KQED (2026-09-30) says UL offers 'just one existing certification' for plug-in solar. The 1,200 W limit comes from Utah law and SB 868, not from UL.

findings.label: SB 868 limits
findings.value: 1,200 W maximum aggregated AC output per dwelling; no DC limit; no battery provisions; certified as a plug-in PV system by UL or equivalent; certified anti-backfeed isolation; effective 2027-01-01, sunsets 2030-01-01
findings.source_title: SB 868: The Plug Into the Sun Act | California Balcony Solar
findings.note: Cited rival; already known, included for context.

findings.label: Cycle life basis (the 80% vs 70% footnote)
findings.value: 4,000 cycles to 80% capacity; Anker's comparison column says 'Other Power Station' is 4,000 cycles to 70%
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: The battery spec table says only '4000 Cycles'. The 80% basis appears in the comparison section. The page says 'Data based on Anker internal testing.'
